story_plan.thesis: The dated September 16 decision and September 17 implementation are distinct: three announced administered settings specify operational instructions, while they do not establish observed market rates or bank/customer pass-through.
story_plan.lead_direction: Orient the reader to the September 16, 2026 decision and next-day effective date, then use the exact three-setting comparison to explain the implementation document. Keep original statement SOURCE_2 separate from implementation SOURCE_1; neither is a new current decision.
story_plan.countercase: An announced operational framework alone does not prove actual execution, effective funding conditions or deposit/loan-rate transmission. The packet supplies settings, not a measured pass-through test or asset-price cause.
story_plan.watchpoint: A later separately admitted official implementation instruction or documented operation would test what changed after these dated instructions; an observed-market-rate or bank-cash transmission claim needs its own exact dated evidence. No later outcome is supplied.

rows.support_excerpt: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 percent, effective September 17, 2026.

rows.label: Standing overnight repo
rows.support_excerpt: "Effective September 17, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 4.0 percent. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.75 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day.
